是的，该前提**正确**。

根据提供的来源（MSF超声手册2018版，第278页，第23.3.2节“Consolidation”）明确指出：

> “Alveolar consolidation appears as an area of poorly defined dark, i.e. hypoechoic, lung tissue resembling liver called hepatization. Within the consolidation, hyperechoic punctate areas can be seen corresponding to air in the bronchi: a so called ultrasound air bronchogram. **Collapsed lung segments can resemble consolidation sonographically and may not have air bronchograms.**”  
> （肺泡实变表现为边界不清的低回声肺组织，类似肝脏，称为“肝化”。实变区内可见高回声点状影，对应支气管内气体，即超声空气支气管征。**塌陷的肺段在超声上可类似实变，且可能无空气支气管征。**）[1][2]

此外，图像下方的文字说明（图7下方的23.3.2节内容）也重复了这一观点：
> “Collapsed lung segments can resemble consolidation sonographically and may not have air bronchograms.” [1]

因此，题干所述“塌陷的肺段在超声上可能类似于实变，且可能没有空气支气管征”**完全符合所提供资料的描述**。

Figure 8: Consolidation
Images (A) and (B) shows smaller subpleural consolidations surrounded by confluent B-lines.
Images (C) and (D) shows large areas of consolidation also referred to as ‘hepatization’ due 
to the liver-like appearance. In (C) the arrow marks the consolidated right lower lobe (LUNG), 
clearly demarcated from the liver (LIV) by the domed diaphragm (DIA).
Note the resemblance in appearance between consolidated lung 
(with bright area = bronchograms) and the liver.
Caution: It is very easy to mistake the liver or spleen for consolidation located close to these 
organs and vice versa. Hence, the thorax should be clearly identified with the ultrasound by 
locating the diaphragm and visualizing the consolidated lung above and the liver or spleen below 
the diaphragm.

The figure shows the other appearance of the interstitial syndrome
